claims.claim: Sealed final evaluation: mean 90%-level interval score of EB-IRT is 0.1449 (primary cases P1-P6, 0.4 synthetic/0.6 real).
Baseline interval scores in the sealed evaluation: naive Wilson 0.2202, Bonferroni-Wilson 0.1974, resampling 0.2461.
EB-IRT aggregate coverage 0.929, mean width 0.129, RMSE 0.0348, signed bias 0.0121.
Naive aggregate signed bias is 0.0366, i.e. the naive estimate exceeds fresh-question accuracy by about 0.037; EB-IRT removes about two thirds (0.0121).
Evaluator qualification outcome is 'qualified' with status 'completed'; all replications completed (fraction 1.0).
Null-control absolute bias 0.0173 and constant-world error 0; null-control coverage averaged over N1 and N2 is 0.929 (N1 0.971, N2 0.887).

Seed-level spread over eight seeds: EB-IRT interval score sd 0.0040, naive 0.0234, Bonferroni 0.0036, resampling 0.0251; EB-IRT lower than each baseline in all eight seeds with paired differences 0.075, 0.053, 0.101.

Replay-derived (not evaluator-recorded) baseline diagnostics: naive Wilson coverage 0.713 (sd 0.048) and width 0.109; Bonferroni-Wilson coverage 0.962, width 0.190; resampling coverage 0.748, width 0.104 (aggregate over P1-P6). The evaluator records only baseline interval scores and the naive bias; the replay reproduced those recorded values exactly (max abs difference 0), and the other replayed quantities are unchecked against any record.
Naive bias on real exhaustive cases falls with N: 0.051 (N=60), 0.022 (N=200), 0.009 (N=600).

Final-pool configuration accuracies range from 0.107 to 0.166 (task manifest); naive optimism at N=60 (0.051) is of the same order as the spread of configuration pool accuracies (0.107 to 0.166); no inference about reported advantage over alternatives.
Naive bias in null worlds: 0.067 in N1 vs 0.049 in P1; 0.034 in N2 vs 0.022 in P3.
Searcher effect on naive bias: P2 0.054, P4 0.025 vs P1 0.049, P3 0.022; matched paired differences +0.004 (sd 0.012) and +0.003 (sd 0.008); aggregated naive bias 0.036 for both searchers.
Per-case EB-IRT vs naive interval scores: P1 0.150 vs 0.264, P2 0.155 vs 0.300, P5 0.192 vs 0.303; reductions of 37-48%; coverage 0.96, 0.96, 0.98.

P4: EB-IRT 0.156 vs naive 0.161 and Bonferroni 0.165; wins in six of eight seeds; bias 0.031 vs 0.025; coverage 0.89 (slightly below nominal, within about one standard error over eight seeds; seed sd about 0.03). P6: all Wilson-style reporters 0.096; coverage 0.83 (seed sd 0.05), clearly below nominal.
Exhaustive-search restricted aggregate: EB-IRT 0.1406, resampling 0.1405, naive 0.2166; halving cases: resampling 0.3916 vs EB-IRT 0.1556.
Resampling is slightly better than EB-IRT in P3 (0.109 vs 0.116), P5 (0.174 vs 0.192) and N2 (0.102 vs 0.111); EB-IRT better in 2, 1 and 1 of 8 seeds.

Replay-derived (resampling bias and coverage are not evaluator-recorded; replay reproduced the recorded baseline interval scores and naive bias exactly): resampling over-corrects under halving with bias -0.067 (P2) and -0.031 (P4), and coverage 0.44 and 0.61; aggregate resampling bias -0.0209.
EB-IRT signed bias positive in five of six primary cases (0.009-0.031) and -0.002 (sd 0.010) in P1.

Controls: N1 EB-IRT coverage 0.971, interval score 0.128 vs naive 0.354 (naive coverage 0.47); N2 EB-IRT coverage 0.887, score 0.111 vs naive 0.218 and resampling 0.102; Z1 interval [0,0.02], score 0.020 vs naive 0.026 and Bonferroni 0.059.
Width factor kappa ranges from 1.43 to 1.63 across the evaluated cases (computed from the reporter's own function).

Development-setting variants (4 seeds): EB-IRT interval score 0.1480, coverage 0.915, width 0.124; config-by-subject variant 0.1519, coverage 0.893; bootstrap pivot variant 0.1562, coverage 0.77, width 0.085; baselines 0.2321 (naive), 0.1961 (Bonferroni), 0.2732 (resampling).
Three reporter variants were evaluated once each in the development setting; all three were scored.
Evaluator-recorded wall-clock time averaged 6.2 s per seed (250 episodes, reporter calls plus scoring), about 50 s over the eight sealed seeds; 2000 episodes in total.
Interval score is a proper scoring rule minimized by the 5% and 95% predictive quantiles.
Related work: adaptive data analysis, reusable holdout, Ladder, post-selection inference, inference on winners, empirical Bayes, bootstrap optimism, prompt search and LLM evaluation (qualitative).
